approved: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Defined Benefit Income Streams) Bill 2015

The bill reintroduces schedule 1 from the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Fairer and Sustainable Pensions) Bill, capping the deductible amount for defined benefit income streams at 10% from 1 January 2016, with military and veterans' affairs pensions excluded, to achieve $465.5 million in further budget savings—adding to $3.5 billion already passed by the Senate.

Labor supported the Defined Benefit Income Streams Bill but criticised the $2.4 billion pension cuts it stems from, which lower asset test thresholds, double the taper rate, and affect 330,000 retirees nationally—including 8,410 part-pensioners in Chisholm. Labor proposed instead saving $14 billion by reducing superannuation tax concessions for balances over $1.5 million, and criticised the Greens for backing the cuts in return for only an inquiry extension, with Prime Minister Tony Abbott confirming no changes to super concessions.

Labor reluctantly supports the bill capping the deductible amount from the pension income test at 10 per cent, but argues the Abbott government has damaged the economy, doubled the deficit, and broken its promise of no pension cuts. The speaker cites 330,000 pensioners set to lose up to $8,000 for singles or $14,000 for couples, and quotes National Seniors and ACTU criticism of the cuts.

The speaker criticised the government for introducing retirement income legislation piecemeal rather than holistically, and argued that the government broke pre-election promises by scrapping the low-income super co-contribution, freezing compulsory super guarantee increases, and reversing tax on high super accounts, while failing to define a fair retirement income.

The speaker argued that the opposition must state whether they would reverse the assets test rebalance measure passed by the Senate, noting the Leader of the Opposition failed to give that commitment, and commended the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Defined Benefit Income Streams) Bill 2015.
Social Services Legislation Amendment (Defined Benefit Income Streams) Act 2015
